gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of video each recorder fits on one card: on a 256 GB microSD at top bitrate, the 4K recorders (ClonerAlliance UHD Pro, Zowietek ZowieREC at 50 Mbps) hold about 11.4 h; the 1080p RecDual Dongle (30 Mbps) about 19 h; Hauppauge's own 128 GB ≈ 16 h figure works out to about 32 h; and the HyperDeck Shuttle HD (157 h per 1 TB in H.264 1080p59.94) to about 40 h.
standout_why: I compared the four pages ChatGPT cited that I could open: cloner-alliance.com UHD Pro (gives 'Up to 50Mbps' and 'selectable 8/16/24/32/50 Mbps', and says only that 4K24 records 'twice as long' as 4K60), the AVerMedia ER330 product page (gives max 1080p60 and storage limits, but no recording bitrate and no hours), streameez.com HD PVR Pro 60 (price, weight and size only), and the cloner-alliance.com RecDual Dongle page (30/16/4 Mbps, no hours). None turns bitrate into hours per card or file size per hour. The two maker statements that do give hours, Hauppauge's support FAQ (128 GB ≈ 16 h) and Blackmagic's '157 hours … on a 1 TB card', were not among ChatGPT's results. The cited ER330 datasheet PDF could not be read as text, so I could not confirm or rule out a table in it.
decides: It confirms the pick split rather than changing it. Buyers who need 4K pay in storage: at 50 Mbps a 4K30 recorder (UHD Pro, ZowieREC) fills a 256 GB card in about 11 h, roughly 4.5 GB per hour. That is about 40% less recording time than the 1080p60 RecDual Dongle at its 30 Mbps max (19 h), and about a third of the 32 h Hauppauge states for the HD PVR Pro 60. For unattended or scheduled long recordings, a 1080p unit or a lower bitrate setting is the better fit: the ZowieREC's 12 Mbps default gives about 47 h per 256 GB, and the UHD Pro's 8 Mbps minimum about 71 h. The page should add one line telling shoppers to plan on a 1 TB+ USB drive for multi-day 4K recording.
